transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-26
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood), Evan (CTO Arcadia), Priya (Legal), Samir (Procurement), Talia (Platform)

Auto-generated Summary:
Arcadia is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid LLM deployment. Primary asks: privileged key management/KMS, VPC connectivity, data residency for health PII, SLA for 99.9% p99 latency and dedicated throughput for peak windows, and clear pricing for both hosted and dedicated reserved capacity. Legal wants DPA clarifications and a pilot-scoped MSA amendment. Team agreed to share pricing matrix, compliance pack, and run a technical bench with sample traffic.

Topics:
- Entitlement and SLA tiers (hosted vs dedicated)
- KMS / privileged keying and egress controls
- DPA redlines and data residency assurances
- Pilot scope, metrics, and timeline
- Cost tradeoffs: latency vs unit cost (batching/quantization)

Action items (auto-gen): see metadata section

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood, Maya our SE, and Luis on solutions. Evan, Priya, Samir, Talia, you there?
[00:12] Evan (Arcadia CTO): Yep, here. Thanks, Jordan. We wanted to focus today on entitlements and the SLA routing logic — how you handle dedicated pools versus hosted fallbacks when capacity spike, and also KMS/privileged key flow.
[00:28] Maya (Redwood SE): Great, we'll cover both. Quick context check — are you planning to start with a hosted pilot or go straight to dedicated reserved capacity?
[00:36] Samir (Procurement): From procurement's lens, we prefer hosted to start for speed, but finance wants a TCO for both. Also legal will need stricter DPA terms if production handles PHI.
[00:50] Priya (Legal): Yes, PHI. Our DPA exceptions list is long; we need clarity on data-at-rest encryption, key ownership, and audit logs. We also need an SLA that includes auditability, not just uptime.
[01:05] Jordan (Redwood AE): Totally reasonable. We can do hosted pilot with a path to Dedicated. For PHI we usually recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS; Redwood supports KMIP and cloud KMS integrations. Note: some of the terminology in our docs might say "keying" or "privileged keying" — that's the KMS flow.
[01:22] Talia (Platform Eng): When you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean we keep keys in our KMS and Redwood does not see them? How does tokenization/ecryption - sorry - encryption happen for inference?
[01:34] Maya (Redwood SE): Short answer: yes, with Private and certain Dedicated configs, keys stay in your KMS/HSM; Redwood never stores plaintext keys. There's an envelope encryption flow: we pull ephemeral creds for host-side operations but the long-term key material stays in your KMS. There's a small handshake and additional latency (2-10ms on hot paths) but it's usually negligible compared to model latency.
[01:54] Evan (CTO): Hmm okay, that latency note is important — our SLO for conversational patient triage is tight. p95 ~ 120ms, p99 < 400ms. We need to understand quantization and batching impacts too.
[02:07] Luis (Redwood): On that SLO, dedicated pools with GPU packing give more predictable latency; hosted can route to cheaper variants but we can set routing policies (latency-first for production routes, cost-first for batch jobs). We'll share perf profiles.
[02:23] Samir (Procurement): Can you share the committed throughput options? We need price bands for 100K tokens/day, 1M tokens/day, and burst windows. Also any egress fees if KMS is cross-region?
[02:35] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes — action: I'll send a dedicated vs hosted TCO and the pricing grid with egress buckets. Note that egress is per-region and depends on private networking; I'll itemize typical fees.
[02:48] Priya (Legal): About the DPA, one clause we need clarity on is data deletion and audit logs. If we run a pilot using masked PHI, we still want a contractual guarantee around retention windows and forensic logs.
[03:01] Maya (Redwood SE): We have retention controls and per-tenant log exports. For Private deployments, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. For hosted, we provide audit snapshots, and we can add custom retention via the enterprise add-on. There might be a small cost.
[03:20] Talia (Platform Eng): Also: network—we need VPC peering or private link. Does Redwood support direct VPC peering, or is it private link or site-to-site? Performance and egress costs differ.
[03:31] Jordan (Redwood AE): We support VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, and on-prem connectors. We'll include connectivity diagrams.
[03:40] Evan (CTO): On the SLA side, we want clarity on failover behavior. If your routing sends traffic to a cheaper variant during capacity crunch, what's the guarantee on semantic equivalence and functional fallbacks? We can't have patient-care path degrade to a smaller model silently.
[03:55] Maya (Redwood SE): Good point. Redwood's rollout policies allow pinning routes to a model family and version; fallback can be configured per-route to either block requests or route to a compatibility-model with a label that denotes lower-quality. You can enforce hard blocks for production. For pilot we can show both behaviors.
[04:13] Priya (Legal): We also want to understand indemnity and data breach clauses in the MSA. Are there standard carve-outs for customers processing regulated health data?
[04:22] Jordan (Redwood AE): We have redlines that enterprises typically suggest. We'll share our standard MSA and a DPA addendum. For PHI, our Private offering with customer keying is recommended; legal team usually accepts that as mitigant for many SOC2/PCI-style asks.
[04:38] Samir (Procurement): What about escrow? If we run Dedicated or Private and need continuity, is there an escape hatch?
[04:45] Luis (Redwood): We do have an optional data & model escrow for certain enterprise contracts — it's not standard but it's an add-on in the mid-enterprise tier. We'll note that in the pricing doc.
[04:58] Speaker 1 (noise / mis-attributed): uh uh — can you share the SH-- the SOC2 scope?
[05:05] Maya (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 type II report and a security pack. Note that some service names in the pack have older synonyms — e.g., our "K-V cache" in docs sometimes appears as "K-B cache" in transcriptions — ignore that.
[05:21] Evan (CTO): For the pilot, we want to validate: throughput (tokens/s), p95/p99 latency, and correctness/regression on a small eval set. Is that something you can run on our behalf or do we need to bring the tests?
[05:32] Maya (Redwood SE): We can run bench tests if you provide a representative sample workload and synthetic traffic pattern. We can also run a side-by-side on your tenant; recommended is to do two runs — a host pilot to check integration, then a dedicated bench to validate SLOs.
[05:48] Talia (Platform Eng): On the connectivity test — would Redwood need inbound network from our side? We prefer not to open inbound from internet.
[05:55] Luis (Redwood): No inbound required if you set up PrivateLink or a peered VPC with route tables. We'll coordinate network handoff doc.
[06:05] Priya (Legal): A quick legal nuance — data residency: some EU patients' data must remain in EU. Does Redwood support region pinning of data and model execution?
[06:15] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes, region pinning is supported for both Hosted (via regional endpoints) and Dedicated/Private. We'll document region-latency tradeoffs and egress implications.
[06:25] Samir (Procurement): Cost question — how much of the cost delta between hosted and dedicated is fixed vs variable? Finance wants to understand break-even for 6/12/24 month commits.
[06:35] Jordan (Redwood AE): Dedicated amortizes fixed infra and gives lower per-token cost at high volume but requires commit. We'll show 6/12/24 month scenarios in the TCO spreadsheet.
[06:46] Evan (CTO): A more technical question — how do you guarantee warm KV caches on dedicated pools during burst windows? We saw regressions on other vendors when KV caches were cold.
[06:58] Maya (Redwood SE): We support prefix caching and checkpoint warmers. For dedicated pools you can reserve warm instances and hold KV cache snapshots across pods. If you need strict p99 we recommend an autoscale buffer and keepalive policy.
[07:13] Talia (Platform Eng): Does that require custom engineering? 
[07:16] Maya (Redwood SE): Not really — it's config + runbook. We can provide suggested autoscale policy templates.
[07:25] Priya (Legal): On the DPA redlines — can you accept a 90-day delete window for pilot logs, and then a move to 30-day for production?
[07:33] Jordan (Redwood AE): We'll need legal review, but that's a fairly common path. We'll flag the DPA items we expect to negotiate.
[07:40] Evan (CTO): Ok let's talk timeline: we want a two-week hosted pilot starting mid-February and a dedicated bench in late February assuming pilot looks good. Can Redwood commit to that cadence?
[07:51] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes — tentative. Action: I'll book a pilot kickoff once I send the pricing and security pack.
[07:59] Samir (Procurement): Anything special on billing terms? Net-30 standard? Or do you need upfront for Dedicated?
[08:06] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hosted is Net-30. Dedicated often requires a commitment and may have an upfront or monthly billing schedule per contract. We'll outline options.
[08:16] Speaker 1: (short cross-talk)
[08:20] Luis (Redwood): One more note for the bench: please include one or two representative long-context calls — that affects memory and kernel choices and can change perf numbers significantly.
[08:33] Talia (Platform Eng): Good point, our patient dialog can hit 2k tokens at times.
[08:38] Maya (Redwood SE): That will affect batching and KV flows; we can tune quantization profiles and model variant selection. We'll include recommended quantization levels for your workload.
[08:51] Priya (Legal): On egress and transfer — if we keep data in EU, are there any third-country transfer clauses we should be aware of?
[08:59] Jordan (Redwood AE): We'll surface any third-party sub-processors and the flow. For EU residency preserved in-region, third-country transfer should be minimal, but we'll confirm with privacy.
[09:10] Evan (CTO): Ok, last thing — we might run a short compliance Q&A with your security team. Can we get 30-45 minutes next week for that?
[09:19] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes — Maya and Luis can join. I'll propose slots.
[09:25] Samir (Procurement): Recap then?
[09:27] Jordan (Redwood AE): Recap: Redwood to send pricing matrix + TCO scenarios, security pack (SOC2, KMS runbook), MSA + DPA templates, and pilot connectivity doc. Arcadia to send data classification, expected monthly token volumes, and confirm pilot participants. Then schedule bench run week of 2025-02-10.
[09:46] Priya (Legal): We'll also flag any DPA exceptions and come back with redlines by 2025-02-06.
[09:51] Evan (CTO): Sounds good.
[09:53] Jordan (Redwood AE): Great — we'll follow up asynchronously. Thanks all.

Post-call notes (auto): Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/decks/privileged-kms-overview.pdf, pricing spreadsheet (will be attached), security-pack link (SOC2)
